tasks.title: kvm_stat leaders
tasks.statement: Write a function kvm_stat_top(text, n): text is kvm_stat output as lines of "counter name, total, per second" separated by spaces (for example "kvm_exit  120000 3500"). Skip lines whose second field is not an integer (headers, empty lines). Return a list of the names of the n counters with the largest total; break ties by name.
tasks.hint: Split the line with split() and check the second field with isdigit().

tasks.title: perf kvm stat report
tasks.statement: Write a function perf_report(text): text is a perf kvm stat report, where event lines have the form "event name, number of samples, share of samples %, share of time %, ..." (fields separated by spaces, percentages with a % sign). Skip the other lines (headers, empty lines). Return a list of tuples (event name, share of time as a float), sorted by share of time in descending order and by name on ties.
tasks.hint: An event is a line where the second field is an integer and the fourth ends with "%".

tasks.title: Image chain
tasks.statement: Write a function backing_chain(text): text is the output of qemu-img info --backing-chain: blocks with lines "image: name" and (not in all of them) "backing file: name (actual path: ...)". Return a list of image names in the order of the "image:" lines (the current layer on top, the base at the bottom).
tasks.hint: Look for lines that start with "image:".

tasks.title: Resource pressure (PSI)
tasks.statement: Write a function psi_status(text, warn, crit): text is the content of a file from /proc/pressure/ of the form "some avg10=1.50 avg60=0.80 avg300=0.20 total=12345" and (not always) a "full ..." line. warn and crit are thresholds for avg10 in percent. Take the largest avg10 value among all lines and return "crit" if it is not less than crit; otherwise "warn" if it is not less than warn; otherwise "ok". Empty text gives "ok".
tasks.hint: The avg10 value is the number after "avg10=" in the line.

tasks.title: Parsing virsh domstats
tasks.statement: Write a function parse_domstats(text): text is the output of virsh domstats for one machine: a line "Domain: 'name'" and lines of the form "key=value". Return a dictionary "key -> integer" only for lines whose value is an integer (negative values do not occur); skip the other lines and pairs.
tasks.hint: Split lines at the first "=" sign and check the value with isdigit().

tasks.title: Where to start diagnostics
tasks.statement: Write a function first_check(symptom, facts): symptom is the complaint, facts is a dictionary of boolean facts about the machine ("virtio", "vhost", "multiqueue", "cache_none", "pinned", "kvm_access"). Return the code of the first check. slow-net: no virtio - "use-virtio"; otherwise no vhost - "enable-vhost"; otherwise no multiqueue - "enable-multiqueue"; otherwise "profile-exits". slow-disk: no virtio - "use-virtio"; otherwise no cache_none - "cache-none"; otherwise "check-iothread". high-steal: not pinned - "pin-vcpus"; otherwise "reduce-overcommit". no-start: no kvm_access - "fix-dev-kvm"; otherwise "check-nested-and-cpu-model". Any other complaint - "unknown".
tasks.hint: Handle each complaint in its own branch and check the facts in order.

tasks.title: Virtualization flags in cpuinfo
tasks.statement: Write a function virt_flags(cpuinfo): cpuinfo is the text of /proc/cpuinfo; it may contain several cores, each with a "flags : ..." line. Among the flags, find the known virtualization flags: vmx, ept, vpid (Intel) and svm, npt (AMD). The flag hypervisor means you are inside a guest. Return a tuple (a sorted list of the virtualization flags found, without duplicates; whether we are in a guest).
tasks.hint: Collect all flags from lines starting with flags into a set.

tasks.title: The cloud-init configuration file
tasks.statement: Write a function render_user_data(hostname, users, packages): hostname is the machine name, users is a list of [user name, public key], packages is a list of packages. Return text in cloud-config format with these lines (with a newline at the end): "#cloud-config", "hostname: <name>", "users:", for each user "  - name: <name>", "    ssh_authorized_keys:", "      - <key>". If there are packages, add "packages:" and for each "  - <package>". If there are no users, do not output the users section.
tasks.hint: Build a list of lines and join them with a newline.
